item.title: Sources: Jensen Huang disclosed additional affairs beyond the two already reported during his Sunday meeting with Nvidia's board, but was remorseful about them (Wall Street Journal)
Filing: ex-OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan recorded a meeting with foreign government reps and photographed a confidential term sheet with another company (Emmy Martin/New York Times)
Filing: the former OpenAI engineer charged with bugging an exec conference room had dozens of OpenAI meeting recordings, many involving possible trade secrets (Madlin Mekelburg/Bloomberg)
Sources: the US is investigating Iran's possible role in cyberattacks on up to 50 energy tankers via a Fortinet router flaw; Russia is also a possible culprit (Wall Street Journal)
Kalshi pauses operations in Utah, where it has 177K+ users, citing a federal court loss over a state gambling law; Kalshi also faces criminal charges in Utah (Alixel Cabrera/Utah News Dispatch)

item.title: Supertake, which uses AI agents to turn users' market predictions into investment portfolios via Coinbase and Robinhood, raised a $20M seed led by Adjacent (Sarah Perez/TechCrunch)

item.title: Australia-based Myriota, which provides low-cost, low-power satellite connectivity for industrial IoT, raised roughly $40M in the first close of its Series C (Rhiannon Hoyle/Wall Street Journal)
HPE reports Q4 revenue up 50% YoY to $14.5B, vs. $14.3B est., forecasts Q1 revenue above the average estimates but below the highest; HPE drops 6%+ after hours (Dina Bass/Bloomberg)
Zoom reports Q3 revenue up 4.9% YoY to $1.29B, above $1.28B est., enterprise revenue up 8.6% to $805.4M, and forecasts Q4 revenue below estimates (Brody Ford/Bloomberg)
Tech stocks rally as Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO; the Nasdaq 100 jumped 7%, a Magnificent Seven basket rose 8%, CoreWeave 22%, Tesla 11%, and AMD 7% (Jess Menton/Bloomberg)
Anthropic unveils Claude Ship, letting Claude review, fix, and approve GitHub pull requests based on team policies, in beta for Claude Team and Enterprise tiers (Radhika Rajkumar/ZDNET)

item.content:encoded: Would you let a few Claude agents review and ship your code for you?

item.title: Sources: the Commerce Department plans to add Megaspeed to its entity list on Monday, barring US companies from selling chips to the company without a license (Ashley Gold/Semafor)
item.description: US companies will not be able to sell chips to the Singapore-based firm at the heart of the Nvidia scandal without obtaining a license.
item.content:encoded: US companies will not be able to sell chips to the Singapore-based firm at the heart of the Nvidia scandal without obtaining a license.

item.title: Sources: Trump pushed Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang after allies argued he was "too big to fail" for the US economy and a victim of "deep state" maneuvering (Axios)
Sources: Trump and JD Vance were convinced Jensen Huang alone protected American-made open-weight AI models (Reuters)
Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia's headquarters to cheers from employees and said "I'm gonna be a better CEO the second time around" (Geoff Weiss/Business Insider)
item.description: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia's Santa Clara HQ to cheers and chants from employees, apologizing for two weeks of turmoil.
item.content:encoded: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia's Santa Clara HQ to cheers and chants from employees, apologizing for two weeks of turmoil.

item.title: Dutch payment company Adyen says co-CEO Pieter van der Does plans to step down at the end of the year; co-CEO Ingo Uytdehaage will become the sole chief (Sarah Jacob/Bloomberg)
AWS CEO Matt Garman says AI safety can't rely on an "emergency brake" and that the same engineering discipline behind decades of secure systems applies to AI (Matt Garman/About Amazon)
item.description: Most of the practical tools to build trustworthy AI systems already exist, and the industry needs to use them.
item.content:encoded: Most of the practical tools to build trustworthy AI systems already exist, and the industry needs to use them.

item.title: Hacking gang CyberLeek claims it released all files for the Xbox build of GTA VI, including an executable program that could help modders port the game to PC (Michael Kan/PCMag)
item.description: 'Xmas came early,' the CyberLeek gang says. If real, the dumped executable program promises to help the modding community create a PC port for Grand Theft Auto 6 soon.
item.content:encoded: 'Xmas came early,' the CyberLeek gang says. If real, the dumped executable program promises to help the modding community create a PC port for Grand Theft Auto 6 soon.

item.title: Sources: Nvidia board's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang was done without consulting Nvidia's senior leadership, who were only informed at the last minute (Bloomberg)
Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott says Jensen Huang will testify publicly on December 3, focusing on oversight of US export controls (Emily Birnbaum/Bloomberg)
Sources: Musk has told employees SpaceX is falling behind in AI, making it more lucrative to rent out computing than use it to improve SpaceX's own products (New York Times)
Filing: the US DOJ is seeking forfeiture of $1B+ in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance by hackers linked to North Korea (Chris Strohm/Bloomberg)
Sources: Trump directed an effort, led by JD Vance, to push for Jensen Huang's reinstatement, assuring Nvidia's board Huang posed no national security risk (New York Times)
Nvidia's board says it is starting a search to fill a new position, Chief Compliance Officer, reporting to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee (Anhata Rooprai/Reuters)
US lawmakers criticize Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang and say Congress must pass legislation to crack down on US chip exports to China (David Shepardson/Reuters)
President Trump says Jensen Huang "did nothing wrong", Nvidia's board "did ask for assurance on the national security threat", and he spoke to Xi about Huang (Dan Mangan/CNBC)
item.description: President Trump said his administration gave Nvidia's board assurance that Jensen Huang would not be a national security threat if he was reinstated as CEO.
item.content:encoded: President Trump said his administration gave Nvidia's board assurance that Jensen Huang would not be a national security threat if he was reinstated as CEO.

item.title: Source: Trump dialed into Nvidia's board meeting to argue for Huang's return; a US official says he "was totally involved" and "we have to protect our geniuses" (J.D. Capelouto/Semafor)
item.description: Chipmaker’s board said it received government assurances that Huang’s return poses no national security risk.
item.content:encoded: Chipmaker’s board said it received government assurances that Huang’s return poses no national security risk.

item.title: Analysis: GTA VI has sold 44.9M copies, not including unsold retail inventory, with the PS5 accounting for 33.7M units, and generated $4B+ in gross revenue (Rhys Elliott/Alinea)
Amazon agrees to acquire much of startup Decart, including the Decart Optimization Stack and its founding team and AI researchers, a source says for ~$7.5B (Matt Day/Bloomberg)
Nvidia's board says it voted to reinstate Jensen Huang after receiving input from "senior levels" of the US government; a probe into his conduct is ongoing (Tim Bradshaw/Financial Times)

President Trump says Nvidia "made the correct and proper decision", the US "needs Jensen's leadership", and the US AG found no evidence of "unlawful conduct" (Donald J. Trump/@realDonaldTrump@truthsocial.com)
Nvidia's board unanimously votes to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, president, and board director effective immediately, after finding no national security risk (Nvidia Newsroom)
item.description: NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board.
item.content:encoded: NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board.

item.title: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX, alleging Grok Imagine's "spicy mode" violated consumer laws by creating 1.8M+ sexualized images of women and 65+ of children (New York Times)
Q&A with Bret Taylor on his long career, co-founding Sierra, working with ex-Googlers, X's influence, AI call center agents, working as OpenAI chair, and more (Dom Cooke/Colossus)
item.description: A conversation with Bret Taylor, who has achieved nearly every feat in business except the one he says matters most
item.content:encoded: A conversation with Bret Taylor, who has achieved nearly every feat in business except the one he says matters most

item.title: Arm CEO Rene Haas extends his contract through 2033 and will become SoftBank vice chair on December 1; a recruiting firm approached him over becoming Nvidia CEO (Bloomberg)
Marlowe, which develops cloud infrastructure and performance tools to optimize non-Nvidia AI chips, raised a $277M seed led by Accel at a $1.15B valuation (Dina Bass/Bloomberg)
Bret Taylor's customer service AI startup Sierra says it's finalizing a $1.75B+ round led by Lightspeed and Greenoaks at a $30B valuation, up from $15.8B in May (Bloomberg)
Sources: Jensen Huang developed a close relationship with Trump and made lobbying calls to secure AI chip sales to China, which he called a $50B per year market (Ian Duncan/Washington Post)
US ports are facing an escalating volume of cyber threats; the Port of LA logged 120M thwarted attempts in August alone, nearly double its 2023 monthly average (Financial Times)
CrowdStrike agrees to acquire Zscaler, which develops network security tools, for ~$43.9B in an all-stock deal, one of the largest-ever deals in the sector (Bloomberg)
Z.ai launches GLM-5.4, a 750B-parameter flagship model built on its Loop Transformer architecture, reaching intelligence levels comparable to 2T-3T models (Z.ai)
London-based defense simulation software startup Agon raised $70M led by Northzone at a $450M valuation, after emerging from stealth with $30M earlier in 2026 (Mark Bergen/Bloomberg)
President Trump hosted a dinner on Sunday for the top $TRUMP collectors; an analysis finds the entry cost was as low as $518, down from its $55K peak in 2025 (Isaac Arnsdorf/Washington Post)
Chinese civilian and military studies show a growing concern that US AI advances may cut nuclear decision-making to 90 seconds, undermining Beijing's deterrent (Chris Buckley/New York Times)
The National Governors Association proposes a split of AI regulation roles, asking the US government to review AI models while letting states protect consumers (Bloomberg)
A look at AECJ, an Amazon employee group with over 1,000 members that is stepping up efforts to slow Amazon's data center expansion and spark debate over AI use (Rafe Rosner-Uddin/Financial Times)
Boston-based Aevius, whose foundation models analyze patient health using medical records, imaging, and other data, raised a $22M seed led by Insight Partners (Katherine Davis/Axios)
Chinese physical AI startup Simplexity Robotics raised a $100M pre-Series A led by Ant Group, with Alibaba, Tencent, and others joining, at a $1.6B valuation (Saritha Rai/Bloomberg)
Compute Desk, which is building capital markets infrastructure to price, trade, hedge, and clear compute, raised a $45M seed round led by Lightspeed (Lucinda Shen/Axios)
New US chip export rules threaten SEA's data center boom, risking incomplete and abandoned projects and forcing neoclouds to replace their Chinese customers (Bloomberg)
London-based Alecto, which uses AI and legal experts to help consumers understand UK property law, raised $20M in seed funding led by Insight Partners (Kyt Dotson/SiliconANGLE)
item.description: Alecto raises $20M seed funding to make UK property law more accessible to consumers with AI - SiliconANGLE
item.content:encoded: Alecto raises $20M seed funding to make UK property law more accessible to consumers with AI - SiliconANGLE

item.title: South Korean PE firm MBK Partners agrees to take Japan's Wacom private, in a deal valuing the digital pen tech company at ~$860M, with Samsung participating (Kim Woo-young/CHOSUNBIZ)
item.description: MBK Partners agrees to acquire Japans Wacom in 1 trillion won deal
item.content:encoded: MBK Partners agrees to acquire Japans Wacom in 1 trillion won deal

item.title: Alexandr Wang says the Riemann Hypothesis proof shows AI will surpass humans in every field, including AI research, and calls for AI safety and alignment (Alexandr Wang/@alexandr_wang)
Arva AI, which builds AI agents for banks' financial-crime compliance teams and counts Wise as a customer, raised a $20M Series A led by Arthur Ventures (Ryan Lawler/Axios)
TPG and Corpay agree to acquire and take private BILL Holdings, whose cloud-based software lets SMBs automate financial operations, in a deal valued at ~$6B (Pritam Biswas/Reuters)
GPT-6.2 Astra vs. Claude Fable 5.2 hands-on: nearly tied on three custom accounting, coding, and data tasks, but Fable used far more tokens and cost 5x+ as much (Jessica Wachtel/The New Stack)
item.description: GPT-6.2 Astra now costs the same per token as Claude Fable 5.2. In three hard tests, Fable scored slightly higher but cost more than five times as much.

A profile of siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei; while at OpenAI, Dario suggested immersive videogames might ease political strife from AI-induced joblessness (Wall Street Journal)

How Dario Amodei built Anthropic's tightly knit culture with essays, Slack memos, and "Vision Quest" talks, as Anthropic seeds his ideas with opinion-makers (Nitasha Tiku/Washington Post)
After FAA, Microsoft, and bank outages, DNI Jay Clayton says Americans should prepare for "bumps in the road" as systems are upgraded to adapt to the AI age (Garrett Downs/CNBC)

Experts say AI has made planning cyberattacks on industrial equipment faster by helping attackers read manuals and research past accidents more quickly (Tom Wilson/Financial Times)
Current and former officials from the US and other countries describe the Chinese spy agency MSS' campaign to help Chinese companies acquire advanced AI chips (New York Times)
Tesla rolls out FSD v15, featuring a photorealistic rendering of car surroundings; Elon Musk says it is real-time AI video generation without using game engines (Mike Pearl/Gizmodo)

Sources: Alice Huang associate Li Ming, whom Singapore charged with fraud in 2025, was central to smuggling restricted AI chips from Southeast Asia to China (Stu Woo/Wall Street Journal)
Matchmakers say more tech workers fear romantic espionage after the Jensen Huang scandal; an AI companion app pitches "zero espionage" executive girlfriends (Wired)

item.title: Investigation: Alice Huang had ties to gaming firms, alleged Prince Group figures and hundreds of shell companies in a network moving Nvidia chips to China (Financial Times)
Sources: Amazon is nearing a $7.5B deal to buy AI startup Decart; talks are at an advanced stage and a deal could come together as soon as next week (Financial Times)
Rhodium: China's biggest tech companies are set to double capex to $139B in 2026 with AI lab revenue under 8% of it, a gap that may matter more than chip curbs (New York Times)
An interview with Google DeepMind in-house philosopher Henry Shevlin on being hired to work on machine consciousness, human-AI relationships, and AGI readiness (Cristina Criddle/Financial Times)
How quantum computers built from laser-trapped atoms may correct qubit errors more easily than supercooled chips, speeding the race to a usable machine (Cade Metz/New York Times)
NYU's Tristan Buckmaster and Anthropic's Levent Alpöge publish an AI-aided proof of Navier-Stokes blowup, saying it closes a loophole in OpenAI's solution (Peter Hall/Scientific American)
